action_summary: A verification run wrote a second copy of the source it had just verified. Measured on main 5eedc03/64af36c: the surface census row fix_then_regression_test was nondeterministic -- the door passed it 4/4 and the independent oracle 1/4 -- with suite_green True and fixed_value '5' in every run. The oracle's third fact is 'the test the machine added FAILS on the buggy code it was given', measured by reverting app/ to the initial commit and re-running the suite. The suite runs that had just confirmed the fix imported app.calc through _source_env, which declared PYTHONPATH and nothing else, so CPython wrote app/__pycache__/calc.cpython-*.pyc from the FIXED source. `return a - b` and `return a + b` are the same size, the revert landed in the same wall-clock second, the pyc header still matched source mtime+size, and the interpreter executed the fixed bytecode against the buggy source. Reproduced in isolation with a plain git checkout: stale pyc present -> OK, pyc removed -> FAILED (failures=1). The rule now lives at the two points every suite run in the family passes: _source_env declares PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and _run_tests builds the child environment unconditionally, including the extra_env=None case that used to inherit the ambient environment. Measured after: census worker 27 6/6 with the oracle's own copy-ignore removed (1/5 before on the pristine base c64af36c, 2/5 on 5eedc03), census 28/28 three consecutive runs, and four new tests that all fail on the pre-change code.
